response.rationale: R6 uniquely unifies the acute right-sided stroke phenotype with a specific etiology: severely deficient ADAMTS13 activity plus schistocytes and thrombocytopenia indicate thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, and the negative inhibitor with a similar family history favors congenital/familial TTP. R1 identifies the ischemic stroke but does not explain its cause; R3 overstates atherosclerosis in a 25-year-old without vessel-plaque evidence; R4 lacks any raw support; R5 is too broad and is superseded by the specific ADAMTS13 finding; C1 merely adds the acute time window to R1.

rejected.why: Atherosclerosis is unlikely in a 25-year-old; raw hypertension and obesity are nonspecific vascular factors, not demonstrated intracranial atherosclerosis.
Adds only the 6-hour acute window to R1 and does not address the ADAMTS13 deficiency/schistocyte evidence.
Has no raw support span; childhood ITP cannot justify an underlying hypercoagulable stroke mechanism.
Thrombophilia is a nonspecific hypothesis based only on prior/family events and contradicts the more specific ADAMTS13 and schistocyte diagnosis of TTP.
